In 1932, Australia sent soldiers with machine guns to fight an army of birds.
After the First World War, veterans became wheat farmers in Western Australia.
Then about twenty thousand emus came and started eating the crops.
The farmers asked for help. The government sent the army.
A major, two soldiers, two machine guns, and thousands of rounds.
But the emus split into small groups and scattered.
They put a machine gun on a truck. The truck was too slow, and the gun jammed.
After about a month, the army quietly went home.
The major said an army with the stamina of those birds could take on any army in the world.
The emus kept eating the wheat.
